$comment: A ThingTalk-style command grammar for Mac control, after Genie (Campagna/Xu/Lam, PLDI 2019). An agent compiles a natural-language request into ONE typed plan of this shape, which a deterministic runner executes and verifies step by step. The point, straight from the paper: a formal, checkable representation beats a model freehanding actions. A plan either type-checks and runs, or it errors cleanly - it does not silently misfire.

structure.stream: the trigger. when the plan runs. one of: now, every, on_text, on_file, on_calendar
structure.query: reads. gather typed data. never has a side effect. layers 1, 3, 6
structure.action: does. has a side effect. layers 2, 4, 6. anything outbound or irreversible carries confirm:true

streams.name: on_text
streams.impl: poll chat.db or a Hammerspoon watcher

design_principles_from_genie.strong_typing: every param is typed (ref, label, css, handle, date, duration, path). A plan that passes a label where a ref is required is rejected before it runs, not halfway through.
design_principles_from_genie.orthogonal_skills: one query per source, one action per effect. No overlapping verbs that do subtly different things, which is the ambiguity Genie's ThingTalk redesign removed.
design_principles_from_genie.user_mental_model: queries return lists that are implicitly iterated. 'reply to everyone I owe' is one action over the result of one query, not a hand-written loop.
design_principles_from_genie.canonical_form: the runner sorts params and normalizes the plan so the same intent always compiles to the same plan, which is what makes a plan checkable and cacheable.
design_principles_from_genie.confirm_is_a_type: confirm:true is part of the action's signature, not a runtime afterthought. The gate cannot be forgotten because it is in the grammar.

example.request: every morning, text me my unanswered threads from the last day
